record.context_brief: K(pi,1) complement of essential ramification set
record.original_question: Let R^d be the parameter space of monic real degree-d polynomials f_a(x)=x^d+a_1x^{d-1}+...+a_{d-1}x+a_d. Let the essential ramification set be the codimension-2 subvariety of parameters for which f_a has either a real triple root or a pair of complex-conjugate imaginary double roots. Is the complement of this essential ramification set in R^d a K(π,1)-space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathbb{R}^d$ denote the parameter space of monic real polynomials of degree $d$,
$$f_a(x) = x^d + a_1 x^{d-1} + \cdots + a_{d-1} x + a_d, \qquad a = (a_1, \ldots, a_d) \in \mathbb{R}^d.$$
Define the essential ramification set $\Sigma \subset \mathbb{R}^d$ to be the set of all parameters $a \in \mathbb{R}^d$ such that the polynomial $f_a$ has either (i) a real root of multiplicity at least three, or (ii) a pair of complex-conjugate non-real double roots. The set $\Sigma$ is a real subvariety of codimension $2$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$.

Question: Is the complement $\mathbb{R}^d \setminus \Sigma$ a $K(\pi,1)$ space, i.e., is its universal cover contractible (equivalently, are all higher homotopy groups $\pi_k(\mathbb{R}^d \setminus \Sigma) = 0$ for $k \geq 2$)?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a published resolution of this specific question about the complement of the essential ramification set in the space of real degree-$d$ monic polynomials being a $K(\pi,1)$ space. Related work by Vassiliev computes homology of associated coverings and gives complete topological descriptions for $d \leq 5$, but no general $K(\pi,1)$ result for arbitrary $d$ was found. Status appears unverified.

status_evidence.title: On topological invariants of real algebraic functions
status_evidence.snippet: A natural covering responsible for the complexity of the ramification of roots of the general real polynomial equation is considered, and the homology groups of its base are calculated; for equations of degree ⩽ 5, a complete description of the topology of this base is given.
status_evidence.claim: Related results give homology and complete topology only up to degree 5; no general K(pi,1) statement is established.
